title: Code2Bench: Scaling Source and Rigor for Dynamic Benchmark Construction
claim: An end-to-end framework scales both problem source and test rigor through staged filtering, yielding a versioned benchmark with diagnostic outputs.
layout: 2 stacked horizontal bands (Source on top, Rigor below), each flowing left-to-right with icons, pill-shaped method labels and arrows, and outputs at the far right. The crop is cut off on both sides.
description: Two horizontal swimlanes stacked vertically. The top light-blue lane is labeled 'Source' and the bottom light-green lane is labeled 'Rigor'. Each lane is a left-to-right chain of stages connected by thin blue arrows. Each stage has a bold title, a line icon, a dark pill naming the technique, and outlined boxes beneath it. Top lane: acquisition and filtering of GitHub code, then Principled Classification (Scope Graph Analysis, with SC Pool of about 10K and WSC Pool of about 5K candidates), then Semantic Filtering (LLM-as-a-Judge, SC and WSC Candidates). Arrows from there lead to green and orange code-snippet cards for SC and WSC candidates. Bottom lane: test synthesis (property-based testing), then 'The Great Filter' (100% Coverage Gate, with red text saying only about 40% pass), then Benchmark Instantiation (Versioned Benchmark, Multi-Faceted Suite in Py and Java). The outputs are a leaderboard podium icon and a diagnostic fingerprint distribution icon. The crop is cut off at both the left and right edges.

abstract: The evaluation of code-generating Large Language Models (LLMs) is fundamentally constrained by two intertwined challenges: a reliance on static, easily contaminated problem sources and the use of superficial, low-rigor testing. This paper introduces a new benchmark construction philosophy, Dual Scaling, designed to systematically address both limitations. Our approach involves continuously scaling the source of problems from dynamic, real-world code repositories and systematically scaling the rigor of tests via automated, high-coverage Property-Based Testing (PBT). We instantiate this philosophy in CODE2BENCH, an end-to-end framework that leverages Scope Graph analysis for principled dependency classification and a 100% branch coverage quality gate to ensure test suite integrity. Using this framework, we construct CODE2BENCH-2509, a new benchmark suite with native instances in both Python and Java. Our extensive evaluation of 10 state-of-the-art LLMs on CODE2BENCH-2509, powered by a novel "diagnostic fingerprint" visualization, yields three key insights: (1) models exhibit a fundamental performance gap, excelling at API application (Weakly Self-Contained tasks) but struggling with algorithmic synthesis (Self-Contained tasks); (2) a model's performance is profoundly shaped by the target language's ecosystem, a nuance we are the first to systematically quantify; and (3) our rigorous, scaled testing is critical in uncovering an "illusion of correctness" prevalent in simpler benchmarks. Our work presents a robust, scalable, and diagnostic paradigm for the next generation of LLM evaluation in software engineering. The code, data, and results are available at https://code2bench.github.io/.
